Adipose tissue: Structure, function and metabolism


Structure
Adipose tissue is a special loose connective tissue dominated by adipocytes. The name of these cells is based on the cell’s content of
a large lipid droplet with “adipo” being a combining form derived from the Latin adeps meaning “pertaining to fat.” In adipose
tissue, fat cells are individually held in place by delicate reticular ﬁbers clustering in lobular masses bounded by ﬁbrous septa sur-
rounded by a rich capillary network. In adults adipocytes may comprise approximately 90% of adipose mass accounting only for
